original.target_description: Study 1, undergraduate visual global/local/control priming; breadth of categorization, 3(Typicality) × 3(Processing Style) interaction reported at supplied p. 112 locator.

n.quote: For each of the 10 main studies, 60
n.sample_role: Participants in Study 1; three between-participant priming conditions in the reported ANOVA.
n.exclusions: No Study 1 exclusions reported; analytic inclusion supported by reported F(4,114) and F(2,57), rather than a separate post-exclusion n statement.

replication.target_description: Experiment 1, laboratory students; one-sided independent-samples Bayesian t-test of global versus local priming on mean typicality ratings for 12 fringe exemplars (BOC creativity score).

n.quote: Of the 104 data sets remaining, we used only the first 100 for the final analysis
n.sample_role: Analytic participants, laboratory global versus local conditions (50 per condition).
n.exclusions: 112 recruited; 8 excluded for Navon error rate >25%; first 100 of remaining 104 used according to preregistered protocol.

p.quote: a comparison of global and local group means was not significant (t(98) = 1.233, p = .110).

reported_success.quote: In Experiment 1, our Bayesian analysis yielded a Bayes factor of 1.38, which indicates that both the null and the alternative hypothesis are about equally supported by the data.

notes: Original p. 112 locator identifies the typicality × processing-style interaction. The distinct fringe-exemplar processing-style main effect is printed in Figure 2A, p. 113: F (2, 57) = 8.93; p < .05; it is not paired with the interaction p-value here. Original n=60 is explicitly reported for each main study and consistent with both tests, but no separate post-exclusion analytic-n statement is printed. Original paper title and DOI verified in retrieved full PDF. Replication cached title and author list match supplied reference; cache uses manuscript pagination (results pp. 16–17 and 22–23), rather than supplied published pp. e85/e87 or PDF pp. 6/8. Replication p-values are the authors’ frequentist one-tailed comparisons of the same conditions, outcome and analytic sample as the Bayesian tests; no p-value is assigned to the Bayes factor itself. Experiment 1 interim conclusion (manuscript p. 17) also says results do not match FD2012; uninformative records the authors’ specific Bayesian assessment of this experiment.
